questions.prompt: An LDSC intercept substantially above 1 (e.g. 1.15) in a GWAS of a quantitative trait most likely indicates:

options.B: Confounding such as population stratification or cryptic relatedness

questions.prompt: A GWAS of HDL cholesterol (N ≈ 15,000; a highly polygenic trait) has λGC = 1.05 and an LDSC intercept of 1.02. The most appropriate interpretation is:

options.A: The study is confounded and must be discarded

options.C: Principal components must be added until λGC equals 1.00

questions.prompt: In regenie step 2 for a binary trait with 1,500 cases and 13,000 controls, Firth logistic regression is used mainly to:

options.B: Control type I error and bias for low-frequency variants under case-control imbalance

questions.prompt: What does regenie step 1 produce?

options.B: Whole-genome ridge-regression predictions (leave-one-chromosome-out) used as offsets in step 2

questions.prompt: A SuSiE 95% credible set is best described as:

options.A: The set of variants with p < 5e-8
options.B: A small set of variants that contains a causal variant for one signal with at least 95% posterior probability, under the model assumptions
options.C: All variants with r² > 0.95 to the lead variant
options.D: The 95% confidence interval of the lead variant's effect size

questions.prompt: SuSiE reports 4 credible sets at a locus, using in-sample LD from about 14,000 people. The best statement is:

options.B: At least 4 independent causal signals are proven
options.C: There may be several signals; this needs confirmation (e.g. conditional analysis or replication), and low-purity sets are unreliable
options.D: The result is meaningless because SuSiE cannot use in-sample LD

questions.prompt: Before computing principal components for ancestry, variants are LD-pruned and long-range LD regions such as the MHC are excluded. Why?

options.B: So that the PCs capture genome-wide ancestry structure rather than local LD patterns

questions.prompt: Why are A/T and C/G (palindromic) SNPs problematic when aligning summary statistics to a target dataset?

options.B: The strand cannot be determined from the alleles alone; allele frequencies are needed
options.C: They cannot be genotyped on arrays

questions.prompt: Which inputs does PRS-CS require?

options.A: Individual-level genotypes and phenotypes of the discovery GWAS
options.B: GWAS summary statistics, the GWAS sample size, an LD reference panel and the target variant list
options.D: A validation cohort with phenotypes, which is always mandatory

questions.prompt: The genome-wide significance threshold of 5×10⁻⁸ corresponds approximately to:

options.A: A Bonferroni correction for about one million independent common-variant tests
options.C: The p-value at which heritability becomes significant
options.D: A threshold specific to East Asian populations

questions.prompt: To convert the observed-scale SNP heritability of a binary trait to the liability scale, you need:

options.B: The sample prevalence (case fraction) and the population prevalence

questions.prompt: A PRS weight file has about one million variants, but only 20-40% of them are found in the target genotype data. The most appropriate first step is:

options.A: Proceed; the match rate does not matter
options.B: Check genome build, variant ID format and allele coding, and keep in mind that a partial score can perform worse
options.C: Rescale the remaining weights by the inverse match rate

questions.prompt: In a case-control GWAS, the Hardy-Weinberg test is often restricted to controls (or uses a lenient threshold in cases) because:

options.B: A true disease association can itself cause departure from HWE in cases
options.D: HWE cannot be computed in cases

questions.prompt: LDSC gives an SNP-heritability of 0.26 with standard error 0.08 (z ≈ 3.3) for N ≈ 14,500. The best statement is:

options.B: The estimate is imprecise (z < 4); treat it as a rough estimate with a wide confidence interval

questions.prompt: ALDH2 rs671 (Glu504Lys) is notable in Korean GWAS of HDL cholesterol and alcohol-related traits because:

options.A: It is common in East Asians but nearly absent in Europeans
options.B: It is a rare variant found only in Africans
options.C: It lies in the MHC region

questions.prompt: A minor allele count filter (e.g. MAC ≥ 20) before association testing exists mainly because:

options.A: Rare variants have no biological effects
options.B: Test statistics for very rare variants are unstable and can be miscalibrated

questions.prompt: Distance-based clumping of GWAS hits (±500 kb around each lead variant) and statistical fine-mapping differ in that:

options.B: Clumping defines loci for reporting; fine-mapping estimates which variants within a locus are likely causal
